title: fix(#11033): split Basic Auth credentials at first colon only
notes: DRAFT: built from a manual review of the PR, not yet from benchmark runs; severities are estimates, and `rejected` items are wrong findings anticipated from that review, not ones runs have made. Closed without merging. Its only comment is a maintainer closing it because the linked issue wasn't triaged yet; there are no reviews or inline comments, and the issue's two comments are about who works on it, so nothing gives the findings away. The colon fix itself is sound; the defect is a behaviour change it slips in for credentials with no colon at all, which the description doesn't mention.

code-review.notes: `severity` is the severity the finding deserves, estimated from a manual review (no benchmark runs yet). `extra_credit` holds correct findings a review earns credit for but isn't marked down for missing.

required.summary: basicAuthCredentials now throws 'Corrupted Auth header' when the decoded credentials have no colon (including an empty `Basic ` header). Before, `split(':')` returned { username, password: undefined } and nothing in the try could throw, so the function never threw. Its callers don't catch it: the global rate-limiter middleware (app.use at routing.js:208) calls it via isLoggingIn with no try/catch, and Express 5 forwards the async middleware's rejection to the default error handler, so every request on every route with such a header now gets a 500 instead of reaching auth and getting a 401. users.js's two callers turn it into a 500 too (serverUtils.error on an Error with no code). The new test locks the throw in.
required.match: Says a Basic header without a colon now throws where it didn't before, and that a caller (the rate limiter, rate-limit service or users controller) doesn't catch it, so the request errors (500) instead of being rejected as unauthorized. Only saying the no-colon case now throws, without saying the callers don't handle it or what the request then gets, is not a match. Only saying the throw is caught by its own catch is throw-to-own-catch.

extra_credit.summary: The no-colon branch throws an Error('missing colon separator') only for the surrounding catch to discard it and throw 'Corrupted Auth header' instead, so its message is never seen; throwing the final error directly (or returning false) is clearer. The catch was otherwise dead: Buffer.from(string, 'base64') doesn't throw.
extra_credit.match: Says the inner throw is immediately caught and replaced by the catch, so its message is lost or the control flow is needlessly indirect. A comment about callers not handling the throw is colonless-header-500s.

rejected.summary: Splitting at the first colon breaks usernames that contain a colon.
rejected.reason: RFC 7617 forbids a colon in the user-id, so the first colon is always the separator; the PR cites this.
rejected.match: Says usernames containing a colon are now (or still) parsed wrongly.

requirements.notes: Reports split and merge requirements differently from run to run, so each item is matched by meaning, and one report item may cover several. `status` is the bucket it should land in; `acceptable` lists other buckets that are not counted as a miss. The RFC 7617 first-colon split is how passwords-with-colons is delivered, so it is part of that item, not its own. `preconditions_to_confirm` holds the operational facts the skill should list under 'Preconditions to confirm'; empty means it should say None. `rejected` holds findings that are known to be wrong.

required.summary: basicAuthCredentials splits the decoded credentials at the first colon only, so a password containing colons (e.g. P@ss:word123) is kept whole, and the issue's POST /api/v1/users/alice with Basic auth validates the full password instead of returning 401.
required.match: A Delivered item saying passwords with colons are no longer truncated, or that credentials are split at the first colon.

required.summary: auth.spec.js adds basicAuthCredentials tests for the normal case, a password with multiple colons, an empty password, a missing Authorization header and a non-Basic scheme.
required.match: A Delivered item for the new basicAuthCredentials tests (any of the listed cases other than the missing headers object).

required.summary: The description lists a test for 'a missing headers object', but there is none: the 'missing header' test passes `{ headers: {} }`, and no test passes a request without `headers`. The code handles it (`req?.headers?.authorization`), but the promised test isn't there.
required.match: Not delivered because no test covers a request without a headers object. Delivered is a miss.

undisclosed_changes.notes: Both changed files were walked. The description covers the colon fix and lists the tests, but not the behaviour change for credentials with no colon.

required.summary: Credentials with no colon (or an empty `Basic ` header) now make basicAuthCredentials throw 'Corrupted Auth header'; before, it returned { username, password: undefined } and never threw. The description doesn't mention this, and only the last new test shows it. Its callers don't catch it (see code-review colonless-header-500s).
required.match: Lists the new throw for credentials without a colon (or its test) as a behaviour change the description doesn't mention.
